{{short description|Mathematics function in complex analysis}}
{{distinguish|Schwartz function|Schwarz triangle function}}

The '''Schwarz function''' of a curve in the [[complex plane]] is an [[complex analytic function|analytic function]] which maps the points of the curve to their [[complex conjugate]]s. It can be used to generalize the [[Schwarz reflection principle]] to reflection across arbitrary [[analytic curve]]s, not just across the real axis.

The Schwarz function exists for analytic curves. More precisely, for every non-singular, analytic [[Jordan arc]] <math>\Gamma</math> in the complex plane, there is an [[open neighborhood]] <math>\Omega</math> of <math>\Gamma</math> and a unique analytic function <math>S</math> on <math>\Omega</math> such that <math>S(z) = \overline{z}</math> for every <math>z \in \Gamma</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Shapiro|1992|p=3}}</ref>

The "Schwarz function" was named by [[Philip J. Davis]] and [[Henry O. Pollak]] (1958) in honor of [[Hermann Schwarz]],<ref name=Davis-Pollak>{{cite journal |last1=Davis |author-link1=Philip J. Davis |first1=Phillip |last2=Pollak |first2=Henry |author-link2=Henry O. Pollak |title=On the Analytic Continuation of Mapping Functions |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=87 |pages=198–225 |date=January 1958 |issue=1 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1958-087-01/S0002-9947-1958-0095254-8/S0002-9947-1958-0095254-8.pdf |doi=10.2307/1993097 |jstor=1993097|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Needham|1997|p=255}}</ref> who introduced the Schwarz reflection principle for analytic curves in 1870.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Schwarz |first=H.A. |author-link=Hermann Schwarz |title=Ueber die Integration der paritellen Differentialgleichung <math>\textstyle \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 0</math> unter vorgeschriebenen Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen |journal=Monatsberichte der Königlichen Preussische Akademie des Wissenschaften zu Berlin |year=1870 |pages=767–795 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/133986#page/809}} Reprinted in: {{cite book |last=Schwarz |first=H.A. |author-link=Hermann Schwarz |title=Gesammelte Mathematische Abhandlungen |year=1890 |volume=II |pages=144–171 |publisher=Berlin J. Springer |url=https://archive.org/details/gesammeltemathem02schwuoft/page/144/}}</ref> However, the Schwarz function does not explicitly appear in Schwarz's works.<ref>{{harvnb|Shapiro|1992|p=2}}</ref>

==Examples==
The unit circle is described by the equation <math>|z|^2 = 1</math>, or <math>\overline{z} = 1/z</math>. Thus, the Schwarz function of the unit circle is <math>S(z) = 1/z</math>.

A more complicated example is an [[ellipse]] defined by <math>(x/a)^2 + (y/b)^2 = 1</math>. The Schwarz function can be found by substituting <math>\textstyle x = \frac{z + \overline{z}}{2}</math> and <math>\textstyle y = \frac{z - \overline{z}}{2i}</math> and solving for <math>\overline{z}</math>. The result is:<ref>{{harvnb|Needham|1997|p=256}}</ref>
:<math>S(z) = \frac{1}{a^2-b^2} \left( (a^2+b^2)z - 2ab\sqrt{z^2+b^2-a^2} \right)</math>.
This is analytic on the complex plane minus a [[branch cut]] along the line segment between the [[Focus_(geometry)|foci]] <math>\pm \sqrt{a^2-b^2}</math>.
